correctness.rationale: At prime level the Legendre-character correlation gives K_p=J+Q, QJ=JQ=0 and QQᵀ=pI−J, hence absolute determinant p^((p+1)/2). In F_p[t]/(t^p) the generating function has first nonzero coefficient at r=(p−1)/2, by the polynomial sums for binomial(x²,j); the coefficient there is −1/r!. This gives exactly r positive p-valuations. Their total is r+1, so precisely one is 2 and the rest are 1; these data suffice since all valuations counted are positive integers. Also (K_p−I)/2 is invertible modulo p because its polynomial has nonzero constant term. At depth two simple-root lifting of units and the count of p roots of zero give K_(p²)=pI+2H_p⊗J_p in coset order. The lift-reference/difference basis splits off pI of size p(p−2) and leaves the submitted two-by-two block matrix. Local pivoting on 2H_p gives Schur complement −p²K_p(2H_p)^−1, hence I_p⊕p²K_p over Z_(p). The original triangular form has determinant p^(p²) det K_p, ruling out other primes. The factors, rank and exponent are therefore valid for every odd p, including the empty p³ block at p=3.
residual_risks: Bounded numerical checks concern local valuations; the algebraic determinant proves the absence of torsion at all other primes.

value.rationale: This is the natural integral convolution operator for the square map on the first nonfield cyclic prime-power ring, not an arbitrary graph or choice of matrix entries. Its complete primary profile, notably the single p⁴ factor and the different p² and p³ multiplicities, is not accessible from the determinant or field case alone. The depth-two integral decomposition explains these specific invariants rather than extrapolating examples.
residual_risks: No general classification at depths three and higher or for other quadratic operators is established.
